recentItems.title: In conversation with legendary musician Yvonne Chaka Chaka
recentItems.description:
From becoming one of South Africa’s pioneering black television performers to building a career in music, acting, business and humanitarian work, Yvonne Chaka Chaka  has consistently used her platform to create opportunities for others. Through her Princess of Africa Foundation, she has championed health and education, while her advocacy has focused strongly on the empowerment of women and girls. As we celebrate Women’s Month, we sit down with the Princess of Africa to reflect on a remarkable journey.

recentItems.title: Expressions | Women in Politics | 31 August 2026
recentItems.description:
Women’s participation in politics is a fundamental part of a democratic and equal society. Women make up approximately half of the world’s population, yet they have historically been underrepresented in political institutions and decision-making structures. 

Women’s Month provides an important opportunity to recognise the achievements of wo Women’s political participation is also important for younger generations. When girls see women occupying positions of authority, they are more likely to view leadership and political participation as possibilities available to them. 

Female political leaders can therefore serve as role models and demonstrate that leadership is not determined by gender. Men in political leadership, reflect on the challenges they continue to experience, and encourage greater participation by women and girls in public life.

recentItems.title: Couple faces 35 charges of fraud, money-laundering and corruption
recentItems.description:
The bail hearing of Tshwane Metro Police officer Peter 'Gagash' Nonyane and his attorney wife, Charlotte Tibana, is expected to resume in the Polokwane magistrate's court in Limpopo. The couple faces 35 charges of fraud, money-laundering and corruption. They are accused of defrauding five deceased estate accounts of more than four-million rand. The accused have been in custody since their arrest two weeks ago. For more we cross to our reporter Rendani Raliphaswa.

recentItems.title: Two of the four men arrested in connection with the murder continue with their bail application
recentItems.description:
Two of the four men arrested in connection with the murder of former boxing world champion, Zolani "Last Born" Tete, are expected to continue with their bail application in the Mdantsane Magistrates' Court in the Eastern Cape today. Among those appearing is a wheelchair-bound 22-year-old, who is alleged to be the mastermind behind the crime. He faces charges of murder and attempted murder of a passenger. 

In his previous appearance, the court dismissed his application to be transferred to a public health facility due to his medical condition. 
The other two accused, who have abandoned their bail application, are expected back in court on the 13th of October. For more on this we cross live to our reporter Abongile Jantjies.

recentItems.title: Matlala and 4 others on trial for attempted murders
recentItems.description:
The trial-within-a-trial in the attempted murder case of Vusimuzi Cat Matlala and four others continues in the Johannesburg high court. Matlala is accused of orchestrating the failed assassinations of his former girlfriend, Tebogo Thobejane, businessman Joe Sibanyoni, and music producer Seunkie Mokubung, popularly known as DJ Vettys. SABC News Reporter, Neria Hlakotsa is there, let's cross to her live.
